facts.fact: The Matabeleland South provincial health team reports 110 of the province's 153 health facilities (71.9%) with Impilo fully functional, 138 (90.2%) with the network installed, 112 (73.2%) activated with trained users and 15 (9.8%) with no coverage, on data from its May 2025 meeting; one province, all facility types, not primary clinics alone.
The same study cites the Ministry of Health and Child Care's 2024 mid-term review for Manicaland Province at 88% coverage and 68% functional, giving no numerator or denominator; one province.

The study, led by the provincial health team with the ministry, says the Ministry of Health and Child Care launched the Impilo EHR system and runs its rollout mandate; no date is given for this, so the document's published date is used.

The study says Impilo was launched as part of the National eHealth Strategy 2021-2025, which aims at nationwide digitisation of health records, and cites a 2024 mid-term review of that strategy; the document's published date is used.

systems.owner: Ministry of Health and Child Care
systems.tiers: Matabeleland South: 138 of 153 facilities across seven districts, urban centres to remote rural clinics; 15 mine, border-post and uniformed-forces clinics excluded from the rollout
one remote site in Matabeleland South

note: The study does not say whether records are entered at the point of care, and gives no breakdown by facility tier. It records 2 sites non-functional for power, 26 awaiting training, and unstable connectivity in Bulilima and Matobo districts; integration of Impilo with LIMS and ELMIS is a recommendation, not a fact.
